mainTopic: Water in a קרפף, and how to permit carrying in the yard in פום נהרא using a לחי
overview: Earlier, the גמרא ruled that water inside a קרפף is treated like planted trees, so it does not ruin the area's status as enclosed for living. אמימר limits this to water that is fit for use. רב אשי adds a limit for deep water covering more than בית סאתים, but the גמרא rejects his limit by comparing the water to a pile of fruit, which never ruins the קרפף however big it is. Then the גמרא tells of a large yard in פום נהרא that opened on one side to the town and on the other to a vineyard path leading to a riverbank. אביי looks for a way to permit carrying there. A wall on the riverbank fails because a מחיצה cannot be built on top of a מחיצה, and a doorframe fails because camels would knock it down. So אביי suggests a לחי at the vineyard path's opening. רבא objects that people would wrongly think a לחי works for any vineyard path, so he places the לחי at the yard's opening to the town instead. Carrying within the town and within the yard is then permitted. Carrying between them is disputed by רב אחא and רבינא.

steps.title: אמימר limits the water rule to usable water
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says the water in the קרפף counts like planted trees only if it is fit for use. If it is not usable, it does not get that status.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: This is only when the water is fit for use. But if it is not fit for use, then no.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר adds a condition to the earlier rule that water in a קרפף is like planted trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water counts like planted trees because people use it, so it serves the needs of living there. If the water is not drinkable or usable, it does not serve living. So it does not get the protected status, and carrying in the קרפף becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: This is only when (a formula that adds a condition to an earlier rule)
They are fit / suitable
Use (here: drinking and normal household use)
An enclosed open area outside the house, such as a storage yard

steps.confusionAlert: אמימר is not saying water in a קרפף is always a problem. He is only limiting the earlier lenient rule to water that people can actually use.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
This is only when [the water] is fit for use,
but if it is not fit for use — no.
phrases.notes: Then it is not treated like planted trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the earlier ruling, on the previous amud, that water is like planted trees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water in a קרפף counts like planted trees only if it is fit for use.

steps.title: רב אשי adds a size limit for deep water
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that even usable water only counts as planted if the deep water does not cover more than בית סאתים. If it does, carrying is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even when the water is fit for use, we only said this rule when its deep part is not more than בית סאתים. But if its deep part is more than בית סאתים, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a second limit on top of אמימר's limit. It is based on the size of the deep water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even usable water could be too big. רב אשי holds that once the deep water (ten טפחים deep) covers more than בית סאתים, it is no longer part of normal living. Then the קרפף loses its status as enclosed for living.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said [this rule] when (a formula that narrows a rule)
In its depth (the area where the water is deep, ten טפחים)
An area the size of two סאה of seed (5,000 square אמות), the size limit for a קרפף
Forbidden (here: to carry)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And even [water] that is fit for use,
we only said [this]
when its deep part is not more than two beit se'a,
but if its deep part is
more than two beit se'a — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וּדְחַזְיִין לְתַשְׁמִישְׁתָּא נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on אמימר's condition and adds a further size restriction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Usable water more than בית סאתים in deep area causes the קרפף to be forbidden.

steps.title: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's limit using a pile of fruit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב אשי's limit is not correct. Usable water is like a pile of fruit, which never ruins the קרפף no matter how large it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is not so. It is just like a pile of fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא itself rejects רב אשי's size limit from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pile of fruit stored in a קרפף is part of normal living, even if it is huge. Usable water is the same. Since it serves living, its size does not matter, so רב אשי's limit is rejected. אמימר's limit (the water must be usable) still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is not so (the statement is rejected)
Just like (a formula that brings a comparison)
A pile of fruit

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: usable water in a קרפף is like planted trees and does not ruin its status, whatever its size. Unusable water does not get this status.
steps.confusionAlert: Only רב אשי's addition is rejected here. אמימר's condition about usable water is not rejected.

phrases.english: And it is not so,
just as it is with a pile of fruit.
phrases.notes: However large the pile is, it does not cancel the residential status.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא, מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַכַּרְיָא דְפֵירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's size limit from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רב אשי's size restriction; אמימר's usability condition remains.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Size does not matter for things that serve living, as with a big pile of fruit.

steps.title: A new case: the yard in פום נהרא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins describing a large yard in פום נהרא. One side opened to the town, and the other side opened to a vineyard path that led to the riverbank.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain yard in פום נהרא. One side opened to the town, and the other side opened to a path between the vineyards. And the vineyard path went up to the bank of the river.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new story. It is only setting up the facts here, and the question and ruling come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This רחבה was larger than בית סאתים and was not enclosed for living. It was connected to the town on one side. On the other side it led to a walled vineyard path that ended at a high riverbank, which counts as a partition. The upcoming question is whether carrying is allowed in this setup.

keyTerms.meaning: An open yard or plaza
Pum Nahara, a town in Babylonia
Side
A path between vineyards
The riverbank, a high bank that can act like a wall

phrases.english: There was a certain yard in Pum Nahara,
one side of which opened to the town,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד גִּיסָא הֲוָה פְּתִיחַ לִשְׁבִיל שֶׁל כְּרָמִים,
phrases.english: and the other side opened to a path between the vineyards,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁבִיל שֶׁל כְּרָמִים הֲוָה סָלֵיק לְגוּדָּא דְנַהֲרָא.
phrases.english: and the vineyard path led up to the bank of the river.
phrases.notes: The bank is ten טפחים high, so it counts as a מחיצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new practical case about a large, unenclosed area connected to partitions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the facts of the case only; no ruling yet.

steps.title: אביי asks how to fix the yard and suggests a wall at the river
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks what can be done to permit carrying in the yard. His first idea is to build a מחיצה at the riverbank.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What should we do? Should we build a wall for it on the riverbank?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a search for a practical fix for the yard and puts forward his first idea. This line sets up the next move, which will test whether the idea works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vineyard path is closed on its sides but open at the river end. If a wall were placed at the riverbank, the path would be closed on all sides. The yard would then no longer be open to an unenclosed area.

keyTerms.meaning: What should we do? (a call for a practical solution)
A wall or partition
The riverbank

phrases.english: Abaye said: What should we do?
Should we make a partition for it on the riverbank?
phrases.notes: This would close off the open end of the vineyard path.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the yard case described in Step 4 and looks for a way to permit carrying there.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical repair will allow carrying in the yard?

steps.title: A wall at the river does not help
steps.stepSummary: The riverbank idea is rejected because a new wall cannot be built on top of an existing wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not make a partition on top of a partition.
steps.whatsHappening: The first idea is knocked down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The riverbank already counts as a מחיצה by itself. The aim was to build a new wall that would count as enclosing the area for living. But a wall built on top of an existing מחיצה does not count as a new partition, so it gives the area no new status and fixes nothing.

keyTerms.term: אֵין עוֹשִׂין מְחִיצָה עַל גַּבֵּי מְחִיצָה
keyTerms.meaning: A partition is not effective when built on an existing partition

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹשִׂין מְחִיצָה עַל גַּבֵּי מְחִיצָה.
phrases.english: One does not make a partition on top of a partition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין עוֹשִׂין מְחִיצָה עַל גַּבֵּי מְחִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposal made in Step 5.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The bank is already a partition, so a new wall on it adds nothing.

steps.title: Second idea: a doorframe at the path's entrance
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests putting a צורת הפתח at the mouth of the vineyard path.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we instead make a doorframe at the mouth of the vineyard path?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries a second fix, and the next step will test whether it holds up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צורת הפתח (two posts with a beam across the top) turns an open gap into a legal doorway. This would close the open side halachically without building a solid wall.

keyTerms.meaning: A doorframe: two posts with a crossbeam, which counts as closing an opening
A path running between vineyards
Mouth or opening

phrases.english: And should we make a doorframe for it
at the mouth of the vineyard path?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַעֲבֵיד לֵיהּ צוּרַת הַפֶּתַח אַפּוּמָּא דִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁל כְּרָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the riverbank idea failed, a new repair is proposed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Would a doorframe at the path's mouth solve the problem?

steps.title: Camels would knock the doorframe down
steps.stepSummary: The doorframe idea fails for a practical reason: camels walking to the river would knock it over.
steps.simpleTranslation: Camels will come and knock it down.
steps.whatsHappening: The second idea is rejected, and the reason is practical rather than a legal rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Camels use this path to reach the river to drink. A doorframe across the path would keep getting knocked over, so it would not last.

keyTerms.meaning: Camels
They throw down or knock over

phrases.english: Camels will come and knock it down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the doorframe proposal from Step 7.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would not survive the camel traffic, so it is not a lasting fix.

steps.title: אביי's solution: one side post at the path's opening
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes that a לחי should be placed where the path opens into the yard. Since it works for the path, it also works for the yard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: Let us put a side post at the opening of the vineyard path. Since it helps the vineyard path, it also helps the yard.
steps.whatsHappening: After two failed ideas, אביי gives his real answer: a single side post.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לחי is a small post that is not in the camels' way, so it will stay standing. It fixes the path, and because of that (מגו), it also counts as closing the yard's open side. One small post solves both problems.

keyTerms.meaning: A side post placed at the edge of an opening
Since (one thing works, the other works too)
A large open yard

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's proposed fix is one לחי at the path's opening. Using מגו reasoning, it would fix both the path and the yard. The next step shows that רבא objects to it.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: לֶיעְבֵּיד לֶחִי אַפִּיתְחָא דִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁל כְּרָמִים,
phrases.english: Let him make a side post at the opening of the vineyard path,
for since it is effective for the vineyard path,
it is also effective for the yard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the two rejected ideas with a workable one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Place a לחי at the path's opening, and it permits both the path and the yard.

steps.title: רבא objects: people will misunderstand
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that people will wrongly think a לחי works for any ordinary vineyard path.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: People will say that a side post works for vineyard paths in general.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's solution. He does not say it fails in this case; he worries it will mislead the public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most vineyard paths are open at both ends, and a לחי would not help them. Here it works only because the river end is already closed. Onlookers would not know that and would wrongly copy the fix elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: They will say (people will draw a wrong conclusion)
In general, ordinary ones

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the לחי fails here. His objection is only that it will mislead people about other paths.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
People will say a side post is effective
for vineyard paths in general.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the solution given in Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if it works legally here, onlookers will wrongly assume a לחי permits ordinary open vineyard paths.

steps.title: רבא's solution: a side post at the opening of the town
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the earlier idea and says to place a לחי at the opening of the town. Because of מגו ("since"), a לחי that works for the town also works for the yard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: We put a side post at the opening of the town. Since the side post works for the town, it also works for the yard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new solution to replace אביי's לחי, which he had just objected to. He moves the לחי to a spot where nobody will learn a wrong lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's objection in step 10 was that a לחי on the vineyard path would mislead people. They would think a לחי fixes any ordinary vineyard path. A לחי where the town's alleyway opens into the yard is a normal, accepted use, so it causes no confusion. The yard then benefits through מגו: once the לחי properly serves the town, it serves the attached yard as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals replacing a rejected approach)
A side post placed at an opening, which allows carrying in an alleyway-type area
The opening of the town
Since / because (if it works here, it also works there)
An open yard (here, the yard in פום נהרא that opens to the town)

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
phrases.notes: אלא shows that רבא is replacing אביי's rejected suggestion.

phrases.english: We make for it a side post
at the opening to the town,
phrases.notes: This is a new location, chosen so that no one learns a wrong lesson from it.

phrases.english: since the side post is effective for the town,
it is also effective for the yard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem רבא raised in step 10 by moving the לחי to a location that does not mislead.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can carrying be permitted in the yard without misleading anyone?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Place a לחי at the opening of the town. Through מגו, it also permits the yard.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic מגו argument: a fixture that properly serves one area can extend its benefit to a connected area.

steps.title: Practical summary: carrying within each area, and the dispute about carrying between them
steps.stepSummary: Carrying within the town is permitted, and carrying within the yard is permitted. Carrying from one to the other is disputed by רב אחא and רבינא: one forbids and one permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore: carrying within the town itself is permitted. Carrying within the yard itself is permitted. From the town to the yard, or from the yard to the town, רב אחא and רבינא disagree. One forbids it and one permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the practical result of רבא's solution. It then notes one case that remains in dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the לחי is in place, each area on its own is clearly permitted. The open question is moving objects across from one area to the other. The text does not give the reasons. It only records that one אמורא forbids this and the other permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore (introduces a practical summary)
To carry / move objects
Itself (within that area alone)
They disagree
One forbids and one permits

steps.whatToRemember: With רבא's לחי at the town's opening, carrying inside the town is permitted and carrying inside the yard is permitted. Carrying between them is a dispute between רב אחא and רבינא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that because each area is permitted, carrying between them must be permitted too. That is exactly the point רב אחא and רבינא argue about.

phrases.english: Therefore:
Carrying within the town itself is permitted.
Carrying within the yard itself is permitted.
From the town to the yard and from the yard to the town,
Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it:
one forbids and one permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws practical conclusions from רבא's solution in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Carrying inside the town and inside the yard is permitted. Carrying between them is disputed: one of רב אחא and רבינא forbids it, and the other permits it.
